ledger.note: 793 BC: 'Established: 793 BC' (infobox; lead 'c. 8th century to 338 BC'). A league 'led by Alba Longa' of 'about 30 city-states and small settlements', 'created for protection against enemies from surrounding areas'; the eight names on Cato's inscription are Tusculum, Aricia, Lanuvium, Lavinium, Cora, Tibur, Pometia and Ardea.
672 BC: Alba Longa, the league's head, 'completely destroyed' by Tullus Hostilius (672-640), its population moved to Rome (year = start of the reign).

notes: New state (the brief: the Latins are missing between the Roman Kingdom and Rome's expansion). The land is Latium Vetus less the Roman Kingdom shape, so the roman-republic dossier's gain of 'the Latin cities and northern Campania' in 338 has a counterpart. Alba Longa's loss (672) mirrors roman-kingdom. Rome's leadership from 358 is not tinted, as the roman-republic dossier has no vassal event for it. Wikidata Q858016 unverified. Revised 2026-10-19 after review: keyframes latin-league_-793 and latin-league_-672 added (the second without the Alba Longa district); the Aricia capital stays a placeholder: both the Latin League and the Aricia pages were opened and neither names a league centre after Alba Longa, so the confidence-1 note says so. Wikidata Q858016 was from memory and could not be checked (wikidata.org unreachable); set to null on 2026-10-19.
